newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX-30 index ends year at days' high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX-30 index ends year at days' high.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index of blue-chip shares closed the last day's trade of the year at a day's high as the bull market continued to prevail and the stronger dollar lifted shares.
The index came off a little as the session went on, but rallied towards the end to close at 2,888.69 points, up 35.81 points or 1.26 percent.
This closing price represents an increase of 28.16 percent on the closing price on the last day in 1995.
Bourse trade underwent a rally in late trade as the index made a series of sharp gains as an options expiry impacted on trade and as dealers sought to settle their books.
Electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index ended for the year at 2,880.07 points, up 20.85 points or 0.73 percent, at around 1300 GMT. The market will reopen again on Thursday.

Dealers said that some of their colleagues did not make it into work because of heavy snow in Germany and that an unwillingness to take up new positions at the end of the year also impacted strongly on volumes.

The strong dollar helped underpin the market over the course of the bourse session. The U.S. currency stood at 1.5564 marks, slightly off earlier levels but still strong enough to boost exporting stocks.
Big volumes of trade were seen in the recently-floated telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG, which ended up six pfennigs at 32.45 marks.
There were also big volumes in industrial giant Daimler- Benz AG which ended up 2.35 marks at 106 marks.
Dealers said that prices reflected year-end activity, such as short-covering, rather than any fundamental issues.
